text.p: The number of Asian "megacities", or cities with a population of over 10 million, will more than double to 20 by 2025 and bring with them problems of congestion and crime, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said.
"The continuing migration from rural to urban areas in Asia will expand the number of megacities from nine to 20 by the year 2025," the ADB said in its annual report issued on Monday.
Over the past 30 years, Asia's urban population had nearly tripled to 1.1 billion from 400 million.
The nine Asian megacities at present were Beijing, Bombay, Calcutta, Jakarta, Osaka, Seoul, Shanghai, Tianjin and Tokyo.
Bangkok, Dhaka, Karachi and Manila would soon join this list, the ADB said.
The report said a major dilemma facing the region was how to mobilise enough resources to ensure an adequate and sustainable quality of life in these overcrowded cities.
It estimated that $20 billion to $40 billion would be needed annually over the next decade to provide adequate services in Asia's giant cities.
"It is difficult to predict what will happen if there are shortfalls in the financing of megacity growth and management," it said.
